description: PART B - retarget ARV to ~Rs.10,000 today, kill the end-of-chart spike, and make the whole arv_candles series continuous and back-matched to a SINGLE anchor that tracks real BTC. USER DECISION (latest steering, confirmed via user_input): today's ARV price should be ~Rs.10,000, launch (2015) small (~Rs.18), chart shape EXACTLY Bitcoin's real 10 years (~560x), proper minute-by-minute recent history, no artificial spike. This supersedes the earlier Rs.1000 target. ROOT CAUSE of the Rs.758/+34027% spike: on live installs the v8 migration moved anchor settings and re-queued backfill, but auto_backfill_step() SKIPS any timeframe whose stored row count already exceeds auto_backfill_floor(tf) - so pre-existing 1m/1D series (computed against the OLD anchor) were advanced past WITHOUT recompute, while fresh ingest writes NEW-anchor minutes -> a right-edge discontinuity and a nonsense sinceLaunchPct. Fix = (1) set the new Rs.10k anchor everywhere, (2) a schema 8->9 corrective migration that force-sets the anchor settings to the new values AND fully rebuilds/rescales ALL arv_candles to the current anchor by re-queuing an UNCONDITIONAL backfill, plus makes backfill overwrite the old rows regardless of row count, (3) fix sinceLaunchPct/stats to be computed consistently against the same base the candles use. MUST NOT re-run the v8 unit rescale (wallets/lots/ledger) - guard on units_rescaled_v8 and the new step touches ONLY candles + backfill scheduling + settings, never unit balances or the append-only ledger. Money invariants preserved: USD is display-only (added in FEAT-004), candles are pure market data (ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, no money).
steps: Compute the new base. baseInr_at_launch = base_btc_usd * base_fx_usd_inr = 277.89 * 63.50 = 17646.02. Real now/launch multiple ~ (BTC_now_usd * fx_now)/(baseInr_at_launch). For BTC ~ $110k and fx ~ 90 that is ~ (110000*90)/17646 ~= 561. To land NAV_today ~= Rs.10,000: arv_base_inr = 10000 / 561 ~= 17.83. Use arv_base_inr = 17.83 (document the arithmetic in a comment). Keep launch_at 2015-07-20, base_btc_usd 277.89, base_fx_usd_inr 63.50 unchanged (real observed anchors, they set the BTC-matched shape). Because NAV_launch == arv_base_inr in the index formula, launch value will read ~Rs.17.83 (this is the honest consequence of tracking BTC's real ~560x; ATH will scale to BTC's real ATH proportion). If the coder finds the live BTC/fx materially different, keep arv_base_inr computed so NAV_today lands near Rs.10,000 and note the assumed BTC/fx in findings.

Update arv-config.js INDEX.arvBaseInr from 1.78 to 17.83 (leave launchMs, baseUsd.BTC, baseFxUsdInr as-is). Update the surrounding comment block that currently explains the '~1.78 -> ~Rs.1000' choice so it explains the '~17.83 -> ~Rs.10,000' choice and the ~560x BTC multiple; keep it honest about the daily/weekly deep-history vs recent-minute limit.

Update api/_schema.php arv_default_settings(): change 'arv_base_inr' from '1.78' to '17.83'. Update the explanatory comment above it (the 'today's price sits near Rs.1000' text) to describe the Rs.10,000 target and the arithmetic. Leave launch_at/base_btc_usd/base_fx_usd_inr unchanged.
Bump ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION from 8 to 9 in api/_schema.php and update the version comment to describe step 9 (corrective anchor + full candle rebuild to the Rs.10k anchor; NO unit rescale).

Add a NEW migration block in arv_migrations() (api/_schema.php) for schema 9, guarded by its own settings flag e.g. 'anchor_recomputed_v9'. When the flag is not set: (a) FORCE-set the four anchor settings to the new canonical values (arv_base_inr='17.83', launch_at='2015-07-20 00:00:00', base_btc_usd='277.89', base_fx_usd_inr='63.50') via UPDATE settings SET svalue=? WHERE skey=? - this repairs installs left in ANY partial state by the v8 migration (v8 only migrated when settings equalled the exact old defaults; v9 is unconditional on the anchor SETTINGS because settings carry no money). (b) Re-queue a FULL candle rebuild: setting_set('auto_backfill_next','1D'); setting_set('auto_backfill_fails','0'); setting_set('auto_backfill_fail_step',''). (c) Set a new flag e.g. setting_set('arv_candles_rebuild_v9','1') that FEAT-002's backfill change reads to force overwrite (see next step). (d) setting_set('anchor_recomputed_v9','1') and add a $done[] line. CRITICAL: do NOT touch wallets, lots, or ledger in this block - unit balances were already rescaled by v8; the money value of a holding = units * NAV must stay put, and since we only change the printed NAV/candles here the coder must NOT re-divide units. Add an explicit comment stating the v8 units_rescaled_v8 flag is left untouched and no unit/ledger rows are modified.

Make backfill actually OVERWRITE the old-anchor candles. In api/_feed.php auto_backfill_step(): the `if ($have >= auto_backfill_floor($tf)) { advance without refetching }` skip is what stranded the old series. Add a guard: when setting_b('arv_candles_rebuild_v9', false) is true, do NOT skip on row count for ARV (non-asset) timeframes - always run backfill_tf() so every ARV timeframe is recomputed against the current anchor via index_price(). Once the ARV chain reaches its end for the rebuild (i.e. auto_backfill_after advances past the last ARV tf into the asset chain 'ETH:1D'), clear the rebuild flag: setting_set('arv_candles_rebuild_v9',''). Keep asset (ETH/SOL/XRP) steps on the normal row-count skip. Keep the existing feed_lock('backfill') and fail-isolation logic intact. backfill_tf() already writes arv_candles with ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE using index_price() over raw BTC USD x fx_curve, so a forced re-run recomputes every historical candle to the current anchor - a continuous, BTC-matched series by construction.

Also force the live 1m tail to be recomputed so the recent minutes match: ingest_prices() already recomputes the current 1m arv_candle via index_price() against the current settings every tick, so once settings are updated the newest minute is correct automatically; the historical body is fixed by the forced backfill above. Confirm (by reading) that rollup_all() derives larger frames from 1m so no stale rolled bucket survives; the forced 1D/1W/1h/etc rebuild plus per-minute rollup covers this. Note in findings that the very newest already-stored rolled buckets refresh on the next tick.

Fix the since-launch / stats math in api/market.php window_stats(): it currently does $base = setting_f('arv_base_inr', 1.0) and sinceLaunchPct = (nav-base)/base. Confirm this is now consistent (nav from the rebuilt candles is on the SAME anchor as base). Change the fallback default from 1.0 to 17.83 to match the new anchor default, and add a short comment that base here MUST equal the anchor the candles were computed with. Also confirm handle_snapshot()'s arvChangePct uses the same base (it reads setting_f('arv_base_inr',1.78) - update that fallback default to 17.83 too for consistency). These fallbacks only bite if the setting is somehow missing; the real value comes from settings.

Grep for any other hardcoded 1.78 / 1000 / old-anchor fallbacks in api/*.php and js/ that should track the new base (e.g. index_price() default args setting_f('arv_base_inr', 1.78), arv_nav default). Update fallback DEFAULTS to 17.83 for consistency but rely on the settings row as the source of truth. Do NOT change base_btc_usd/base_fx defaults.
Run php -l on api/_schema.php, api/_feed.php, api/market.php, api/_money.php and node --check on arv-config.js.
acceptance_criteria: arv-config.js INDEX.arvBaseInr and _schema.php arv_default_settings()['arv_base_inr'] both equal 17.83 (or the coder's documented BTC-consistent value landing NAV_today ~= Rs.10,000).

ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION == 9 and a schema-9 migration block exists, guarded by anchor_recomputed_v9, that force-sets the anchor settings and re-queues a full backfill WITHOUT touching wallets/lots/ledger and WITHOUT re-running the v8 unit rescale.

auto_backfill_step() unconditionally rebuilds ARV timeframes while arv_candles_rebuild_v9 is set, then clears the flag, so old-anchor candles are overwritten with current-anchor values (continuous series, no end spike).
window_stats() sinceLaunchPct and handle_snapshot() arvChangePct are computed against the same base the candles use; stale fallback defaults updated to 17.83.
php -l passes on all changed PHP files; node --check passes on arv-config.js.
No wallet unit balance, lot unit, or ledger row is modified by the new migration (verified by reading the block).
verification: php -l api/_schema.php && php -l api/_feed.php && php -l api/market.php && php -l api/_money.php
Read the schema-9 migration block and confirm it contains no UPDATE/INSERT against wallets, lots, or ledger.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED (all steps). Changes: (1) arv-config.js INDEX.arvBaseInr 1.78 -> 17.83 with rewritten comment explaining the ~560x BTC multiple and honest ~Rs.17.83 launch value / ~Rs.10,000 today. (2) _schema.php arv_default_settings()['arv_base_inr'] 1.78 -> 17.83 with updated comment. (3) ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION 8 -> 9 with a version comment describing the corrective anchor + full candle rebuild (no unit rescale). (4) NEW schema-9 migration block in arv_migrations(), guarded by anchor_recomputed_v9: unconditionally FORCE-sets the four anchor settings (arv_base_inr=17.83, launch_at=2015-07-20, base_btc_usd=277.89, base_fx_usd_inr=63.50), re-queues a full backfill (auto_backfill_next='1D', fails='0', fail_step=''), sets arv_candles_rebuild_v9='1', sets the guard flag. The block calls ONLY setting_set() - verified NO UPDATE/INSERT against wallets, lots, or ledger, and it does NOT touch units_rescaled_v8 or any unit balance. (5) _feed.php auto_backfill_step(): while arv_candles_rebuild_v9 is set, ARV (non-asset) timeframes skip the row-count skip and always run backfill_tf() so old-anchor candles are overwritten via index_price() against the current anchor; the flag is cleared once the ARV chain finishes (next step becomes an asset step 'ETH:1D' or 'done'), on both the skip path and the success path. Asset steps keep the normal row-count skip; feed_lock and fail-isolation logic left intact. (6) market.php window_stats() fallback 1.0 -> 17.83 and handle_snapshot() base fallback 1.78 -> 17.83, both with comments that base MUST equal the anchor the candles were computed with. (7) _money.php index_price() fallback 1.78 -> 17.83. (8) Stale display copy comments updated: _match.php header, home.js and trade.js launch-line comments (1.78 -> 17.83; those JS lines already draw from CFG.INDEX.arvBaseInr, comment-only fix). NOTE: v8 migration internals ($newBaseInr='1.78', F arithmetic, ledger note, 'rescaled to 2015/Rs.1.78') were deliberately LEFT AS 1.78 - they describe the historical v8 rescale that already ran on live installs and must not be altered.

VERIFIED IN SANDBOX: php -l passes on api/_schema.php, api/_feed.php, api/market.php, api/_money.php, api/_match.php; node --check passes on arv-config.js, js/pages/home.js, js/pages/trade.js.

MUST BE VALIDATED ON THE LIVE INSTALL (NOT possible here - no MySQL/exchange/WebSocket): (a) run the schema-9 migration (deploy + a cron/web tick) and confirm the schema_version row reaches 9 and anchor_recomputed_v9=1; (b) let the backfill chain run to completion and confirm arv_candles_rebuild_v9 clears once the ARV chain finishes into the asset chain; (c) confirm NAV today reads ~Rs.10,000 (depends on live BTC/fx - if materially different from BTC~$110k, fx~90, NAV scales proportionally; arv_base_inr is fixed at 17.83 per plan, note assumed BTC/fx if it lands off); (d) confirm sinceLaunchPct is a sane ~560x-ish figure (NOT +34027%) and there is a single CONTINUOUS series with NO right-edge spike; (e) confirm wallet unit balances, lot units, and the ledger are UNCHANGED by the migration (only settings + candles changed). If the live BTC/fx makes NAV land far from Rs.10,000, revisit arv_base_inr per step-1 arithmetic (10000 / ((BTC_now_usd*fx_now)/(277.89*63.50))).
